note: Taxonomy Machine Name adds a machine_name string base field to every taxonomy_term, auto-generated (transliterated slug) from the term name on presave and made unique per vocabulary (appending _0/_1...). There is no configure route. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real property using terms in the existing Tags vocabulary, all namespaced by a 'TMN ' name prefix / tmn_ machine-name prefix: introspection reads back a term's machine_name; execution creates terms and verifies the module generated (or kept) the expected machine_name on the live term. Reset scripts delete the specific namespaced terms so verify fails on empty state and passes only after the agent creates them correctly.

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal taxonomy_machine_name module add to taxonomy terms, and how is the value generated when you don't provide one?
evals.expected_output: It adds a machine_name string base field to every taxonomy term. If you leave it empty, on save it is auto-generated from the term name by transliterating to ASCII, lowercasing, and replacing non [a-z0-9_] characters with underscores, then made unique within the vocabulary.

evals.prompt: With taxonomy_machine_name enabled, how can I load a taxonomy term by its machine name in code, and what token exposes a term's machine name?
evals.expected_output: Use taxonomy_machine_name_term_load($machine_name, $vid) (which does loadByProperties(['machine_name'=>..., 'vid'=>...])) to load a term by machine name within a vocabulary. The token [term:machine_name] outputs the term's machine name.

evals.prompt: In taxonomy_machine_name, what happens if two terms in the same vocabulary would generate the same machine name, and are there any reserved values it rejects?
evals.expected_output: It appends an incrementing numeric suffix (_0, _1, ...) until the machine name is unique within the vocabulary (taxonomy_machine_name_uniquify). The term form also rejects the reserved words add, list, delete and update because they clash with taxonomy route arguments.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a taxonomy term in the Tags vocabulary named 'TMN Known Term'. Using the taxonomy_machine_name module's machine_name property, inspect the live term and report its machine name.
evals.expected_output: The term 'TMN Known Term' has machine_name tmn_known_term (auto-generated by taxonomy_machine_name from the term name). Read it with $term->get('machine_name')->value.

evals.prompt: The Tags vocabulary on this site has two terms, 'TMN Alpha One' and 'TMN Beta Two'. Using the taxonomy_machine_name machine_name property, inspect the live terms and state which term's machine name is 'tmn_special_marker'.
evals.expected_output: 'TMN Beta Two' has machine_name tmn_special_marker; 'TMN Alpha One' has an auto-generated machine name (tmn_alpha_one).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a taxonomy term in the Tags vocabulary named 'TMN Product Launch 2026' and let the taxonomy_machine_name module generate its machine name automatically. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create and save Term(['vid'=>'tags','name'=>'TMN Product Launch 2026']); taxonomy_machine_name's presave hook generates machine_name = tmn_product_launch_2026 (do not set it manually).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a taxonomy term in the Tags vocabulary named 'TMN Explicit Term' and give it the explicit machine name 'tmn_custom_slug' using the taxonomy_machine_name module. Save it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create a Tags term named 'TMN Explicit Term', set its machine_name to 'tmn_custom_slug' ($term->set('machine_name','tmn_custom_slug')) and save; the value is a valid slug so it is kept verbatim.
